earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only Ponelis 1993 (Afrikaans history); no Oorlams grammar/phonology found

sources.citation: Hendricks, Frank. 2016. The nature and context of Kaaps: a contemporary, past and future perspective. Multilingual Margins 3(2): 6-39. Bellville: University of the Western Cape (hdl:10566/5365).
sources.note: Nothing on Oorlams; for Kaaps it lists segmental 'phonological markers' and 'Prosodic Afrikaansification of lexical items and expressions derived from English (back > bek, post office..)' without any word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Afrikaanse Taalmuseum en -monument (commissioned report; author not named in the text, PDF author metadata 'Sybrandus'). 2021. Opdrag: Ontleding van die taalkundige, fonologiese en morfologiese element van Gariepafrikaans (ook bekend as Oranjerivierafrikaans) in die onderhoude wat gevoer is in verskeie dorpe en nedersettings in die Noord-Kaap en Namakwaland (39 places incl. Griekwastad, Campbell, Danielskuil, Kuruman, Prieska, Steinkopf, Pella). Paarl: Afrikaanse Taalmuseum en -monument. 113 pp. (PDF 'Gariepafrikaans 2021', posted 2025).
sources.note: Chapter 2.2.1 'Fonologiese kenmerke' (pp. ~13-28) treats vowels (raising/lowering, unrounding, o/e alternations), diphthongs, consonants and consonant processes (velarisation hoorn>horing, palatalisation kind>tjend, dj- for j-, epenthetic forms anderster/pampier), and 2.2.1.5 argues that Khoekhoegowab click consonants should be counted in the Afrikaans sound system; no section or remark on word stress, accent placement, tone or intonation ('klemtoon' occurs only as beklemtoon = emphasise; 'aksent' once = way of speaking of white residents). Morphology chapter follows (plurals, diminutives, te…

sources.citation: Staphorst, Luan. 2024. Oranjerivierafrikaans, 'n argeologiese genealogie. Deel I-IV. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 68 (doi 10.5842/68-1-938, -939, -940, -941)
sources.note: A complete research genealogy of Orange River Afrikaans 1595-2021; no stress statement. Deel III p. 51 reproduces Hendricks' 2012 typology in which 'Oorlams' is a subvariety of 'Afrikaans van Gauteng / Transvaalse Afrikaans' (beside Bosveldse, Laeveldse, Voortrekkerafrikaans), not of Oranjerivierafrikaans. Deel II pp. 353-379 discusses Rademeyer 1931/1938 on Griqua and Rehoboth Baster Afrikaans; Deel IV cites Wissing 2007 on acoustic correlates of stress in (standard) Afrikaans only.

sources.citation: De Klerk, P. 2021. Baanbrekerswerk oor die geskiedenis van Afrikaans. [Review of] E.L.P. Stals en F.A. Ponelis, So het Afrikaans na Namibie gekom; Hollands-Afrikaans in Namibie voor die koloniale tyd (Windhoek: Gamsberg Macmillan, 2001). Historia 47(2): 778-781. doi:10.17159/hasa.v47i2.1498.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Useful pointer only: 'Ponelis.. is alleen verantwoordelik vir hoofstuk 4. Die nege bladsye van hierdie hoofstuk bevat interessante inligting oor besondere taalverskynsels in vroee Namibiese Afrikaans, wat as 'n deel van die noordwestelike Afrikaanse dialek beskou kan word. Vir nie-taalkundiges is hierdie hoofstuk taamlik tegnies.' So the only linguistic content of Stals & Ponelis 2001 is a 9-page chapter 4 (print only).

sources.citation: Ethnologue 18th ed. (2015), entry 'Oorlams' [oor] (archived 2019-10-09)
sources.note: Nothing. Only: 32,000 speakers (2006); Mpumalanga province; status 6a Vigorous; 'Creole, Afrikaans based'; no references given.

sources.citation: Van Rensburg, Christo. 2013. 'n Perspektief op 'n periode van kontak tussen Khoi en Afrikaans. Literator 34(2), Art. 413, doi 10.4102/lit.v34i2.413
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Historical identity only (p. 6): the Oorlams were 'die eerste beduidende groep sprekers van Afrikaans' north of the Orange River and their language 'Oorlamsafrikaans (Khoi-Afrikaans)' became the mission teaching language in 1806; p. 9 points to Stals & Ponelis 2001: 102-106 for example forms of Oorlam/Baster Afrikaans.

sources.citation: Grimes, Barbara F. (ed.). 2000-2002. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 14th edition, web entry 'OORLAMS: a language of South Africa' (SIL code OOR), archived 2002-11-08; also 17th ed. (2013) web entry 'Oorlams' archived 2014-02-06.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content; no bibliography attached to the entry in any edition seen (14, 17, 18).

sources.citation: Luijks, Catharina Adriana Dimphina Maria. 2000. The realisation of syntactic principles in non-standard Afrikaans: the correspondence of Jan Jonker Afrikaner (1820-1889). PhD thesis, University of Cape Town, Dept. of Linguistics and Southern African Languages. hdl:11427/38932.
sources.note: No phonology content: a generative-syntax study (pronominal paradigm, verb cluster, negation, complementisers) of written letters; the author notes that earlier work (Rademeyer 1938, Links 1983 on Kharkams) dealt with phonological peculiarities whereas hers is syntax only. The only 'tone' passage (ch. 2) is the general creole-prototype criterion ('little or no use of tone to lexically contrast.. monosyllables'), not a claim about this variety; 'stress'/'pitch accent' occur only in footnotes on modern Standard Afrikaans example sentences.

sources.citation: Ponelis, Fritz. 1999. Die oorsprong van Afrikaans (Rosetta Project scan, archive.org rosettaproject_afr_detail-6)
sources.note: Nothing; 'oorlams' occurs only as a Malay loanword in Afrikaans.

sources.citation: Nieuwoudt, Hendrina Petronella. 1990. Variasie binne Oranjerivier-Afrikaans. DLitt thesis, PU vir CHO (NWU), hdl:10394/3780
sources.note: Section 4.2 'Fonologiese variasie' (pp. 47-60) covers vowel raising/lowering, length, reduction, diphthongs, unrounding, breaking, syncope, consonant weakening; word stress is never treated (only 'onbeklemtoonde omgewing' as the environment of weakening, quoting De Stadler 1984:200). 'Oorlams' is not mentioned.

sources.citation: Stoffberg, Pierre. 1990. Die geskiedenis van die Afrikaner-Oorlams met spesifieke verwysing na die lewe van Jager (Christiaan) Afrikaner, 1760-1822. MA thesis, Stellenbosch, hdl:10019.1/67230 (Glottolog ref 147668)
sources.note: Pure history (10 chapters on the Afrikaner-Oorlam clan); no language chapter, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Henning, P.J.P. 1984. Vokaalverplasing in die Afrikaans van die Griekwas van Griekwaland-Wes. Literator 5(1): 75-87. doi:10.4102/lit.v5i1.905 (part of the 1980s Griqua Afrikaans project).
sources.note: A variationist account of vowel lowering and raising ([o]>[open o], [e]>[open e], /a/>[u] etc.) per speaker; accent appears only as a conditioning factor, not as a placement statement: p. 77 word-final /o/ 'selde verlaag word, behalwe waar die woord sintaktiese aksent dra'; pp. 80-81 /a/ raised to [u] only in 'daar' (Olifantshoek) 'en elke keer het dit swaar gedra aan die aksent' and 'Sulke veranderlikes is dikwels gevind by swaarbelaste aksent'. No word-stress rule, no tone; search for klemtoon/klem/lettergreep/sillabe/intonasie otherwise empty.

sources.citation: Rademeyer, John Hubert. 1938. Kleurling-Afrikaans: Die taal van die Griekwas en die Rehoboth-Basters. Amsterdam: Swets & Zeitlinger (from 1931 DLitt).
sources.note: Earliest monograph on the Afrikaans of Griqua and Rehoboth Baster (Oorlam-descended) communities, with phonetic description; the only older primary description of these varieties; not on DBNL (checked author index).

sources.citation: Von Wielligh, G.R. 1925. Ons geselstaal: 'n oorsig van gewestelike spraak, soos Afrikaans gepraat word. Pretoria: Van Schaik (NWU scan, hdl:10394/11289, six PDF parts)
sources.note: No Oorlams section. Deel 2, §38 (Noordwestelike distrikte / Namakwaland), p. 167 item 13 says only 'Verskuiwing van aksent kom meesal voor in plaasname, soos: Rooiwal, Swartberg, Grootklip, ens. Vergelyk ook rooikeel.' (accent shift in compound place names in Namaqualand Afrikaans); Deel 1 pp. ~50-57 explain Hoernle's tone/stress diacritics for Nama loanwords. No word-stress rule.
